A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their complete main texts, Appendices A–D, algorithms, equations, table and figures support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Appendix D reports original simulations comparing Algorithms 1 and 2 under type feedback and Algorithms 3 and 5 under action feedback, with cumulative-regret plots.

after.justification: Appendix D retains these original simulations and their cumulative-regret results in Figures 2 and 3.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–5 remain unchanged. New Section 6.1 sketches adversarial adaptations: multiplicative weights with within-region FTRL for type feedback, and EXP3 with within-region bandit linear optimization for action feedback. These are proposed extensions whose formal verification is explicitly left open.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic Bayesian Stackelberg games under type and action feedback in Appendix D. Adversarial types and follower externalities are newly discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains Algorithms 1 versus 2; Figure 3 retains Algorithm 3 versus the Bernasconi-inspired linear-bandit Algorithm 5. Newly mentioned adversarial algorithms and Bollini et al. are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix D retains L=2, K=6, A=2 and n=2, independent types for the type-feedback comparison, and cumulative regret plotted through 100 rounds. No evaluation procedure or setting is revised.

E4.justification: The independent-type specialization comparison and small-n, small-L action-feedback study are retained unchanged. No new ablation, sensitivity analysis, robustness test or empirical case study accompanies the expanded discussion.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over 2000 simulations with 90% confidence intervals in Figures 2 and 3. No run-count, seed or uncertainty-reporting change is documented.

E6.justification: Figures 2 and 3 contain identical regret curves and retain the findings favoring Algorithm 2 over Algorithm 1 and Algorithm 3 over Algorithm 5. Table 1's regret-bound entries are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 footnote 1 newly states generalization to arbitrary compact convex strategy sets with linear or affine utilities. Section 6.2 additionally states that two type-feedback bounds extend to follower externalities when equilibrium computation is handled. Existing theorem statements and appendix proofs remain unchanged; the new Lemma 4.1 proof sketch restates Appendix B.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution paragraph and opening discussion retain the same central novelty claims, regret guarantees, lower bound and computational conclusions. The added extension discussion does not revise these headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Sections 6.1–6.2 substantially expand the treatment of applicability beyond v1's brief discussion of regret and computational gaps. They discuss adversarial extensions, distinguish which bounds survive follower externalities, and explain why equilibrium responses undermine the existing geometric approach.

D1.justification: The established pseudocode, linear-program formulations, oracle descriptions and simulation details are retained. No implementation settings, hardware information or code/data access instructions are added; the proposed adversarial extensions have no implementation specification.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds Bollini et al. (2026), contrasting its single-follower unknown-utility setting with this work's known utilities and unknown type distributions. Other notable reference changes update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify the best-response mapping, concentration argument and linear-bandit reduction. Section 6 gains two subsections, and affiliation, correspondence and citation formatting change. The overall narrative remains intact, although Section 5 newly duplicates the OFUL sentence.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts the ICLR layout, changing typography, margins, running headers, heading styles, algorithm framing and page composition. Figures are resized and algorithm floats move, including Algorithm 5 within its proof discussion. Table 1 and Figures 1–3 retain their underlying contents.

improvement.justification: The added applicability discussion makes the role of follower externalities clearer and explicitly identifies the adversarial extension as unverified. The main-text proof sketch also improves access to existing reasoning. These modest gains outweigh the duplicated OFUL sentence; the established proofs and empirical evidence are unchanged.
